This drives the optical power requirement, and hence power consumption, on the optical source (oscillator and often optical amplifier). Current technology involves a highly nonlinear optical fiber (HNLF) to broaden the spectrum and a nonlinear bulk crystal for frequency doubling. New technologies based on a Photonic Integrated Circuit (PIC) offers the prospect to substantially reduce this pulse energy (by factor of ten). Demonstration of a packaged, Carrier Envelope Offset frequency (fCEO) detection demonstrator unit with fiber in-coupling and fCEO electrical signalout which shall also take full advantage of any recent development enhancements in the capabilities of integrated photonics.
